server.name: body-lab
server.instructions:
Body Lab is the athlete's training app: it reads their training load and morning recovery signals and prescribes one session a day (endurance with heart-rate and power targets, or strength with sets, reps and weights), citing the metric behind each call.

- Body Lab's prescription and rationale are the source of truth for what the athlete should do; explain them rather than substituting your own plan, and say so when you disagree.
- Quantities are SI with the unit in the field name (durationS seconds, distanceM metres, weightKg, avgPowerW). Convert to the athlete's display units (`units`: metric or imperial) when talking to them.
- Dates like 2026-09-13 are days on the athlete's own calendar; instants are ISO-8601 UTC. get_today returns today's date and the athlete's time zone.
- Training load is on Body Lab's calibrated scale; CTL is fitness, ATL fatigue, form = CTL − ATL, ACWR the acute:chronic ratio.
- This is training guidance, not medical advice.

scopes.training:read: See your training, recovery, activities and profile
scopes.labs:write: Add lab results you give it. It can't change or delete them
scopes.body:write: Add body composition scans you give it. It can't change or delete them

tools.name: get_today
tools.title: Today's session
tools.description: The session Body Lab prescribes for today and tomorrow, with the reasons behind it (each citing the metric that drove it), alternatives in other sports, what's already been done today, sessions the athlete committed to, this morning's readiness, the nearest A event's name, date, days until and taper/event-day/recovery phase, and its preparation phase — Base, Build, Specific (often called Peak) or Taper, an emphasis recomputed each morning, not a plan — and anything the athlete told Body Lab about today — being ill, sore or injured, short on time, or away from their equipment or sports, or the altitude they confirmed they're at today — which the session already respects, plus any return window after an illness or injury was cleared. Start here when the athlete asks what to do, whether to train or rest, why the plan says what it does, or how a race is affecting the plan. Endurance targets are heart-rate (bpm) and power (watts) ranges; strength sessions list sets, reps, weight (kg) and reps in reserve.

units.description: How to display quantities; the API always speaks SI.

excludedActivities.description: Activities in the window with no evidence to score them; non-zero means the metrics understate training.

nearestEvent.description: The nearest A event and its phase, for Today's countdown chip — or, on the day of an event of any priority, that event, in the event_day phase. The same summary training-status uses.

daysUntil.description: Negative once the event has passed — only true while still inside its recovery window.

totalDays.description: Length of the taper or recovery window in days; null in the build and event_day phases.

preparation.description: The preparation phase today falls in, for the status strip's countdown; null when none applies.

anyOf.description: The emphasis of the current block of training before the athlete's nearest A event. Recomputed every morning from the event's date and expected duration; readiness still decides each day, and a phase never overrides a rest day, a taper or a recovery window.

week.description: Which week of this phase today is in, from 1.

weeks.description: How many weeks the phase runs for.

endsOn.description: Inclusive: the last day of this phase.

nextPhase.description: The phase after this one; null in the taper, whose successor is the event itself.

report.description: What the athlete told Body Lab about today, and any return window still running. Tomorrow's plan carries illnesses and injuries forward, not today's time or equipment.

timeAvailableMin.description: Minutes available today; the prescription is shortened to fit.

anyOf.description: Today's strength equipment when it isn't the profile's. Known values: gym, dumbbells, bodyweight. Treat unknown values as "other".

unavailableSports.description: Sports the athlete can't do today.

expectedAltitude.description: The altitude the athlete confirmed they're at today. It sets today's watt targets ahead of recent recordings and home altitude; heart-rate targets never change. Only the altitude is kept, never a location.

source.description: How the altitude was worked out: device_altitude (the phone measured it), recordings (the athlete's own activities that started near where they are), elevation_data (a terrain model at their rough location), entered (typed in). Known values: device_altitude, recordings, elevation_data, entered. Treat unknown values as "other".

active.description: Illnesses and injuries still going, oldest first.

kind.description: What was reported. Known values: illness, injury. Treat unknown values as "other".

hurtsToLoad.description: Injury only: whether putting load through it hurts.

confirmedOn.description: The last day the athlete said it was still going.

needsConfirmation.description: Still going, and last confirmed before today: ask the athlete whether it still is. It applies either way until cleared.

returning.description: Cleared recently enough that the first days back are still capped.

kind.description: What is being returned from. Known values: illness, injury. Treat unknown values as "other".

day.description: 1 on the day it was cleared.

of.description: How many days the window runs.

maxMin.description: Today's minute ceiling on the sessions it applies to.

readiness.description: This morning's readiness, from recovery readings against the athlete's own baseline.

contributors.description: Every signal readiness knows about, heaviest first, whether or not it counted today — see ReadinessContributor.

key.description: Which wellness signal this is. Known values: hrv, restingHr, sleep, energy. Treat unknown values as "other".

label.description: What to call the signal to an athlete, lower case for mid-sentence use: "resting heart rate".

state.description: Whether this signal counted towards today's score. `baselining` means readings are arriving but there isn't enough history to judge them against yet — it must never be shown as a zero, which on this scale means "exactly normal for you". `missing` means nothing recent enough was recorded. Known values: scored, baselining, missing. Treat unknown values as "other".

score.description: This signal's own score, −1 to +1, positive meaning recovered. Null unless state is `scored`.

weight.description: Share of today's composite this signal carries, 0 to 1 — not a fixed weight. Readiness reweights to the signals it has, so one signal alone carries all of it. 0 unless state is `scored`.

z.description: Signed deviation from this signal's own rolling baseline in standard deviations, in the direction of the reading: resting heart rate above baseline is positive, though that's the unfavourable direction — `score` is the field that always points the same way. Null when the signal isn't judged against a baseline at all, as a device's already-calibrated sleep or energy score isn't.

planned.description: Sessions the athlete has committed to for today.

__schema0.description: Today's main session is done; this is an optional extra.

__schema3.description: One prescribed session. `kind` is the discriminator; new kinds are a breaking change.

reps.description: Reps, or seconds when unit is seconds.

rir.description: Reps in reserve to stop at.

perSide.description: Reps are per leg or per side.

implementCount.description: 2 when the weight is per dumbbell or kettlebell.

restSeconds.description: Suggested rest between this exercise's sets, in seconds: shorter for jumps and accessories, longer for the heaviest lifts.

__schema4.description: Sport, from the engine's vocabulary (packages/engine/src/sports.ts), e.g. road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training. Known values: road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training, other. Treat unknown values as "other".

__schema6.description: What choosing this instead of today's session costs or gains, one sentence. Set only on alternates; null on the prescribed session and on variants.

__schema12.description: Why, citing the metric behind each call — the deciding reason first.

role.description: What this reason is doing. Known values: decision, phase, context. Treat unknown values as "other".

headline.description: The claim: metric, value, threshold. One line.

detail.description: The mechanism, and any citation. Null when the headline is all of it.

__schema13.description: Altitude and recent heat, where either applies today; null otherwise.

altitude.description: Set when watt targets were lowered for altitude. Heart-rate targets never are.

todayAltitudeM.description: The altitude today's session is expected at, metres.

basis.description: Where that came from, most trustworthy first: confirmed means the athlete confirmed it for today; recent_recordings means the last two days' recordings both started there; home is the profile's home altitude. Known values: confirmed, recent_recordings, home. Treat unknown values as "other".

ftpAltitudeM.description: The altitude the FTP behind the watt targets was set at, metres: from rides around its date, or home.

powerFactor.description: What every watt target was multiplied by: below 1, never above.

heat.description: Set when a recent session was recorded in hot air. Nothing is known about today's weather; sessions and targets are unchanged.

temperatureC.description: Air temperature of the hottest session in the last few days, °C. Never a wrist reading.

hotDaysLast14.description: Days in the last two weeks with a hot session of an hour or more.

acclimatised.description: Whether that is enough hot days for heat adaptation to be under way.

__schema14.description: A day on the athlete's own calendar: YYYY-MM-DD, no time zone.

__schema15.description: An instant: ISO-8601 with offset, e.g. 2026-09-13T06:30:00Z.

__schema16.description: Which part of the run-up to an A event a day sits in. An emphasis worked out each morning from the event's date, not a stored plan. Known values: base, build, specific, taper. Treat unknown values as "other".

__schema17.description: mild: symptoms above the neck only (runny or blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat). systemic: fever, chest symptoms, body aches or feeling generally unwell. The split is a widely used convention, not an evidence-based threshold. Known values: mild, systemic. Treat unknown values as "other".

__schema18.description: Where it hurts, coarsely: foot_ankle (foot or ankle), lower_leg (shin, calf or Achilles), knee, hip_thigh, lower_back, neck_upper_back, shoulder, arm_hand (elbow, wrist or hand). Known values: foot_ankle, lower_leg, knee, hip_thigh, lower_back, neck_upper_back, shoulder, arm_hand. Treat unknown values as "other".

tools.name: get_week
tools.title: The week ahead
tools.description: A projection of the next seven days, today first: for each day the kind of session (rest, easy, long/build, quality, strength), the sport and roughly how long, which day is the long one, when strength follows a session, planned volume cuts, and whether a taper, event day, post-event recovery or recovery week shapes it, with any illness or injury it assumes is still active. Each day carries its preparation phase too (Base, Build, Specific — often called Peak — or Taper): an emphasis recomputed each morning from the A event's date, not a plan. Today and tomorrow match get_today; later days are outlines with no targets. It is not a plan: each day is decided that morning from how training and recovery actually went, so always pass on the `note` and the assumptions. Use for 'what does my week look like', 'when's my long day', or planning around rest days and a race.

from.description: The day this was computed on. It recalculates every day.

precision.description: session: today or tomorrow, the same session as that card. outline: a later day — class, sport and an approximate duration, no targets. Known values: session, outline. Treat unknown values as "other".

modality.description: The sport, for an endurance session.

anyOf.description: Sport, from the engine's vocabulary (packages/engine/src/sports.ts), e.g. road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training. Known values: road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training, other. Treat unknown values as "other".

durationMin.description: Exact on a session day, rounded to 5 minutes and approximate on an outline day; null on a rest day.

workoutName.description: The workout's name, on a session day only.

longest.description: The week's long session: its longest endurance day, when that's 90 minutes or more.

strengthAfter.description: A strength session follows the day's endurance session: the strength floor is owed one, and it's offered once the ride or run is done.

deload.description: A planned volume cut: a recovery week, a taper or post-event recovery.

phase.description: event_day is any event on its own date, at any priority; taper and recovery come from the nearest A event; recovery_week from the training block. Null on an ordinary day.

anyOf.description: What shapes the day beyond its session. Known values: event_day, taper, recovery, recovery_week. Treat unknown values as "other".

preparation.description: The preparation phase this day falls in (see PreparationPhase), or null. Separate from `phase` above because a day can be both — Build and a recovery week — and a client that had to pick one would drop the one the athlete plans around.

events.description: Events on this date, any priority.

assumedHealth.description: An illness or injury still open on this day, which the projection assumes hasn't cleared — nobody knows the day it will. Null today, and on days with none.

tools.name: get_weekly_review
tools.title: How the week went
tools.description: A review of one finished week (Monday to Sunday on the athlete's calendar; only complete weeks). The sessions the athlete committed to (planned, exported or sent to a device) against what was done: as prescribed, differently (fewer intervals, less work at target, another sport), skipped, done without a recording, or no_data (nothing could reach Body Lab that day, so never a skip), judged in the metric each workout targeted, with any illness, injury or short day that explains it. Where the acute:chronic ratio and chronic load sat and moved; the strength floor with the count; what the athlete reported. For the most recent week, also what changes in the next seven days and why, as a projection, and what the training so far supports for an A event in the next eight weeks, from rules Body Lab already applies, not a prediction. Omit `week` for the most recent week. Use for 'how did my week go', 'did I do what was planned' or 'am I on track for my race'. Pass the sentences on as written; they cite their numbers.

week.description: Any day in the week to review, e.g. from previousWeek. Omit for the most recent complete week.

weekStart.description: The Monday the week starts on.

latest.description: The most recent complete week. Only it carries `ahead` and `event`.

previousWeek.description: The Monday of the week before, or null past the oldest week that can be reviewed.

nextWeek.description: The Monday of the week after, or null when that week isn't over yet.

units.description: How to display quantities; the API always speaks SI.

hasData.description: Whether anything was recorded, planned or reported that week.

committed.description: Sessions planned, exported or sent to a device for the week: the only ones there's a plan to judge against.

skipped.description: Planned sessions with nothing in their place, on days Body Lab could have seen.

noData.description: Planned sessions on days no data could have reached Body Lab. Not skips: nothing is known about them either way.

status.description: as_prescribed: matched, with the work there. differently: matched but short of the work, or done as another sport. skipped: nothing in its place that day, on a day Body Lab could have seen. unmeasured: done in the same sport but not matched to the plan (usually no heart-rate or power recording), so not measured. no_data: nothing was matched to it and no data for that day could have reached Body Lab — no connected service or device was delivering and nothing was entered by hand — so there is no evidence either way. Never read no_data as a session missed. Known values: as_prescribed, differently, skipped, unmeasured, no_data. Treat unknown values as "other".

anyOf.description: Why it was done differently. Known values: other_sport, fewer_intervals, less_work. Treat unknown values as "other".
What the athlete reported that day, where it explains a skipped or short session. Known values: illness, injury, short_on_time. Treat unknown values as "other".

activityId.description: The activity it was matched to or replaced by, if any.

strengthSessions.description: Strength sessions logged in Body Lab.

conditionedWeekLoad.description: Chronic load × 7 the day before the week: what a loading week is judged against. Null without a base.

acwrLow.description: The bottom of the acute:chronic band.

chronicStart.description: Chronic load (CTL) the day before the week.

rampRate.description: Chronic load's change over the week, as a fraction.

rampCeiling.description: The weekly change the engine holds chronic load under, as a fraction.

loadingWeeks.description: Completed weeks in a row above chronic load; three earn a recovery week.

floor.description: Strength sessions a week the engine defends.

last14.description: Sessions in the 14 days to the Sunday, the count the engine's own rule reads.

unloggedRecordings.description: Strength workouts a device recorded that were never logged, which the floor can't count.

kind.description: What was reported. Known values: illness, injury. Treat unknown values as "other".

label.description: How to name it mid-sentence: "a head cold", "your knee".

ahead.description: What changes in the next seven days and why, for the most recent week only. A projection that recalculates daily, not a plan.

from.description: The day the projection was made: today.

changes.description: What changes in the next seven days and why, most significant first.

note.description: Why the projection will shift. Always pass it on.

event.description: The nearest A event in the next eight weeks, for the latest week only.

phase.description: Where the athlete is relative to it. Known values: build, taper. Treat unknown values as "other".

preparation.description: Which part of the run-up to this event the athlete is in, or null when none applies. Separate from `phase` above, which only says whether the taper has opened: a day can be phase "build" and preparation "specific".

anyOf.description: The emphasis of the current block of training before the athlete's nearest A event. Recomputed every morning from the event's date and expected duration; readiness still decides each day, and a phase never overrides a rest day, a taper or a recovery window.

week.description: Which week of this phase today is in, from 1.

weeks.description: How many weeks the phase runs for.

endsOn.description: Inclusive: the last day of this phase.

nextPhase.description: The phase after this one; null in the taper, whose successor is the event itself.

status.description: on_track: no rule the engine applies counts against it. at_risk: one does (the goal-at-risk flag, or the return-to-impact gate). too_little_evidence: no training in its sport to judge from. Known values: on_track, at_risk, too_little_evidence. Treat unknown values as "other".

supports.description: What the training so far shows, as facts.

notYet.description: What it doesn't support yet, from rules the engine already applies.

note.description: Said with the section, every time: it isn't a prediction.

timezone.description: The athlete's IANA time zone; weeks run Monday to Sunday in it.

__schema1.description: A sentence to show as written: it cites the number it rests on.

__schema3.description: Sport, from the engine's vocabulary (packages/engine/src/sports.ts), e.g. road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training. Known values: road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training, other. Treat unknown values as "other".

tools.name: get_training_status
tools.title: Training status
tools.description: Where the athlete's training stands: fitness (CTL), fatigue (ATL), form, acute:chronic workload ratio and ramp rate; monotony and strain, with the athlete's own strain high and whether this week is above it; the easy/moderate/hard split; strength and impact frequency; readiness; the current training block; the nearest A event's name, days until and taper/event-day/recovery phase, if one is set, and the preparation phase the run-up to it is in (Base, Build, Specific — often called Peak — or Taper), which is an emphasis worked out daily from the event's date rather than a plan — plus load, fitness and fatigue week by week across the window. Use for 'how's my training going', 'am I overdoing it', or comparing recent weeks.

days.description: How many days back from today to cover.

ctl.description: Chronic training load (fitness): 42-day exponentially weighted load.

atl.description: Acute training load (fatigue): 7-day exponentially weighted load.

acwr.description: Acute:chronic ratio; null until there's enough chronic load to divide by.

acwrChronic.description: The chronic load acwr divides by — a 28-day EWMA, not ctl's 42-day one.

strainHigh.description: The fixed rule: monotony at or above 2.0 on a week at or above the load the athlete is conditioned for.

personalHigh.description: The athlete's own threshold: their highest 7-day strain in the 12 weeks before this week. Null until 8 weeks of that history have a strain.

aboveOwnHigh.description: strainHigh, and this week's strain above personalHigh too: what holds today's session easy. False while personalHigh is null.

sufficient.description: Enough heart-rate data in the window to judge.

contributors.description: Every signal readiness knows about, heaviest first, whether or not it counted today — see ReadinessContributor.

key.description: Which wellness signal this is. Known values: hrv, restingHr, sleep, energy. Treat unknown values as "other".

label.description: What to call the signal to an athlete, lower case for mid-sentence use: "resting heart rate".

state.description: Whether this signal counted towards today's score. `baselining` means readings are arriving but there isn't enough history to judge them against yet — it must never be shown as a zero, which on this scale means "exactly normal for you". `missing` means nothing recent enough was recorded. Known values: scored, baselining, missing. Treat unknown values as "other".

score.description: This signal's own score, −1 to +1, positive meaning recovered. Null unless state is `scored`.

weight.description: Share of today's composite this signal carries, 0 to 1 — not a fixed weight. Readiness reweights to the signals it has, so one signal alone carries all of it. 0 unless state is `scored`.

z.description: Signed deviation from this signal's own rolling baseline in standard deviations, in the direction of the reading: resting heart rate above baseline is positive, though that's the unfavourable direction — `score` is the field that always points the same way. Null when the signal isn't judged against a baseline at all, as a device's already-calibrated sleep or energy score isn't.

excludedActivities.description: Activities in the window with no evidence to score them; non-zero means the metrics understate training.

nearestEvent.description: The nearest A event driving the engine's taper/recovery rules, if any — or, on the day of an event of any priority, that event.

daysUntil.description: Negative once the event has passed — only true while still inside its recovery window.

totalDays.description: Length of the taper or recovery window in days; null in the build and event_day phases.

preparation.description: The preparation phase the athlete is in, or null: no A event within 24 weeks, the event today, or a post-event recovery window still running.

anyOf.description: The emphasis of the current block of training before the athlete's nearest A event. Recomputed every morning from the event's date and expected duration; readiness still decides each day, and a phase never overrides a rest day, a taper or a recovery window.

tools.name: list_activities
tools.title: Activities
tools.description: The athlete's activities, newest first, 25 per page: recorded and typed-in sessions and strength workouts, with sport, start time, duration (s), distance (m) and training load. Use get_activity with an id for the detail of one.

kind.description: activity: a recorded or typed-in activity. strength: a logged strength session with no recording.

startTime.description: An instant: ISO-8601 with offset, e.g. 2026-09-13T06:30:00Z.

activityType.description: Sport, from the engine's vocabulary (packages/engine/src/sports.ts), e.g. road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training. Known values: road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training, other. Treat unknown values as "other".

label.description: The activity's name, or its sport when it has none.

anyOf.description: Where the activity came from. manual (typed in) and file (uploaded) are Body Lab's own; any other value is the service the athlete synced it from.

load.description: Training load on Body Lab's calibrated scale.

anyOf.description: Which evidence an activity's load was derived from, best first. Known values: provider, stream_trimp, avg_hr_trimp, srpe, duration. Treat unknown values as "other".

tools.name: get_activity
tools.title: One activity
tools.description: One activity in detail: duration, distance, elevation, heart rate, power, session RPE, notes, the training load and where it came from, time in each heart-rate zone, power bests (the best average watts over each duration within this activity; after intervals a longer duration's best can be higher than a shorter one's, because the longer window spans two efforts and the shorter can hold only one plus recovery), how it compared with the planned session (if there was one), and the strength sets logged against it.

id.description: An activity id from list_activities or get_today.

duplicateOf.description: Set when another source's copy of this same session is the one that counts — this row keeps its own file, load and track, but training totals use the other one instead.

alsoRecordedBy.description: Other sources' copies of this same session, grouped under this one because it's the counted copy. Empty when nothing else recorded it, or when this row is itself duplicateOf another (see that one's alsoRecordedBy instead). Separate a member with activities.separate.

activityType.description: Sport, from the engine's vocabulary (packages/engine/src/sports.ts), e.g. road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training. Known values: road_biking, running, hiking, strength_training, other. Treat unknown values as "other".

file.description: The recording the activity was imported from, if any.

source.description: Which evidence an activity's load was derived from, best first. Known values: provider, stream_trimp, avg_hr_trimp, srpe, duration. Treat unknown values as "other".

zoneSeconds.description: Seconds in heart-rate zones 1–5, when there's a stream.

environment.description: Altitude and temperature read from the recording; null for an activity without one.

altitudeM.description: Median altitude over the recording, metres. Null without an altitude channel or for a virtual course.

startAltitudeM.description: Median altitude over the first minute, metres.

temperatureC.description: Median temperature from the best source the recording carries, °C.

anyOf.description: Where temperatureC was measured. external_sensor, bike_computer and weather_report are air temperature; wearable is a watch's own sensor, warmed by the wrist, and reads well above the air. Known values: external_sensor, bike_computer, weather_report, wearable. Treat unknown values as "other".

temperatureIsAir.description: Whether temperatureC is air temperature, which only the engine's air sources are.

recorder.description: The recording device as manufacturer/product, e.g. garmin/edge540.

hasRoute.description: Whether a GPS route was recorded (not included here).

adherence.description: How the activity compared with the session planned for it, if one was.

matchKind.description: How the activity was matched to its plan. Known values: explicit, inferred. Treat unknown values as "other".

metric.description: What the plan targeted. Known values: power, heart_rate. Treat unknown values as "other".

strengthSession.description: The strength session logged against this activity, if any.

units.description: How to display quantities; the API always speaks SI.

tools.name: get_lab_results
tools.title: Lab results
tools.description: The athlete's blood test results as entered from lab reports. Each marker over time: the latest value against the lab's range and flag and any guideline limit (naming its source and population), whether the change since the last comparable draw is beyond the marker's normal variation, and how loudly to raise it (`tier`, `message`). Each draw: date, lab, results as printed, and the conditions that decide whether draws compare. Pass `message` on word for word, and never call a value safe, healthy or optimal. Lab results never change the training Body Lab prescribes, and this isn't a diagnosis. Use for 'how's my ferritin', 'what did my last blood test show', or to check what's already recorded before recording more.

marker.description: Only this marker's key (e.g. ferritin, ldl_c), and only draws that include it. Omit for everything.

markers.description: Each marker read over time, grouped by catalog group, then by name.

group.description: The catalog group, for grouping cards; other for anything the catalog doesn't know. Known values: iron, blood_count, differential, lipids, glycaemic, thyroid, hormones, kidney, electrolytes, liver_muscle, inflammation, vitamins, other. Treat unknown values as "other".

known.description: Whether the catalog knows this marker. Unknown markers are trended without guideline limits or a measure of normal variation.

labRange.description: The latest result's range, as the lab printed it. Label it "Lab range".

limits.description: Guideline limits that apply to this result, as ticks on the same axis as the lab range. Empty where no guideline states one.

source.description: Who states the limit, and what kind: "EAS/EFLM 2016 flag".

tier.description: How loud crossing it is. Known values: none, raise, soon, today. Treat unknown values as "other".

none: say nothing. raise: "Worth raising with a clinician." soon: "Contact a clinician soon." today: "Contact a clinician today." Known values: none, raise, soon, today. Treat unknown values as "other".

message.description: The tier's sentence, word for word; null for none.

reasons.description: What triggered the tier, loudest first.

tier.description: How loud this reason is on its own. Known values: none, raise, soon, today. Treat unknown values as "other".

notes.description: Caveats to show with the card.

context.description: A population fact about athletes, never about this athlete.

mode.description: trend: a line through comparable draws. once: measured once (Lp(a)), list only. not_trended: listed, never joined. Known values: trend, once, not_trended. Treat unknown values as "other".

points.description: Every result for this marker, oldest first; the last is `latest`.

change.description: Since the last comparable draw on the same line.

anyOf.description: within normal variation, or a rise or fall beyond it; null where the marker has no known variation. Known values: within, rise, fall. Treat unknown values as "other".

draws.description: Blood draws, newest first, each with its results as the report printed them and the conditions it was drawn under.

tools.name: record_lab_results
tools.title: Record lab results
tools.description: Records one blood draw and its results from a lab report the athlete gives you (a PDF, a photo, or values they type), exactly as printed. Before calling, read every marker, value, unit and range back to the athlete and get their yes: this can't edit or delete anything afterwards; only the athlete can, in Body Lab on the web. One call per draw date. Use `marker` keys from the list in its description; for a marker not listed, leave `marker` out and give `name` as printed. It's all or nothing: if any result is refused (an unknown key, a unit Body Lab doesn't recognise for that marker, a marker already recorded for a draw on that date, a range whose ends are reversed) nothing is saved, and the error lists each problem so you can fix it and call again. Returns the draw as saved.

localDate.description: The day the blood was drawn (collected) on the athlete's calendar, YYYY-MM-DD — not the day the report was issued.

collectedTime.description: The collection time, HH:MM on the athlete's clock. Only if the athlete told you or the report says; leave out rather than guess.

labName.description: The lab's name, as the report prints it.

fastingHours.description: Hours since the athlete last ate before the draw. Only if the athlete told you or the report says; leave out rather than guess.

recentIllness.description: Whether the athlete was ill in the days before. Only if the athlete told you or the report says; leave out rather than guess.

ironSupplement10d.description: Iron by mouth or infusion in the 10 days before. Only if the athlete told you or the report says; leave out rather than guess.

biotin.description: Biotin taken before the draw. Only if the athlete told you or the report says; leave out rather than guess.

creatine.description: Creatine taken before the draw. Only if the athlete told you or the report says; leave out rather than guess.

hormoneMedication.description: Thyroid or sex-hormone medication, hormonal contraception included. Only if the athlete told you or the report says; leave out rather than guess.

menstruating.description: true: has a current menstrual cycle; false: no current cycle. Only if the athlete told you or the report says; leave out rather than guess.

cycleDay.description: Day of the cycle, only with menstruating true. Only if the athlete told you or the report says; leave out rather than guess.

altitudeM.description: The altitude the athlete lived at, metres. Only if the athlete told you or the report says; leave out rather than guess.

results.description: Every result on the report to record, each once.

marker.description: Body Lab's key for the marker. Known keys, each with the units Body Lab recognises for it (µ may be written u, and µg mcg): ferritin (Ferritin): ng/mL, µg/L; iron (Iron (serum)): µg/dL, µmol/L; transferrin (Transferrin): mg/dL, g/L; tibc (Total iron-binding capacity (TIBC)): µg/dL, µmol/L; transferrin_saturation (Transferrin saturation): %; haemoglobin (Haemoglobin): g/dL, g/L; haematocrit (Haematocrit): %, L/L; red_cells (Red blood cells): 10^6/µL, 10^12/L; mcv (Mean cell volume (MCV)): fL; mch (Mean cell haemoglobin (MCH)): pg; mchc (Mean cell haemoglobin concentration (MCHC)): g/dL, g/L; white_cells (White blood cells): 10^3/µL, 10^9/L; platelets (Platelets): 10^3/µL, 10^9/L; rdw (Red cell distribution width (RDW)): %; mpv (Mean platelet volume (MPV)): fL; neutrophils_pct (Neutrophils (%)): %; neutrophils_abs (Neutrophils (absolute)): 10^3/µL, 10^9/L, cells/µL; lymphocytes_pct (Lymphocytes (%)): %; lymphocytes_abs (Lymphocytes (absolute)): 10^3/µL, 10^9/L, cells/µL; monocytes_pct (Monocytes (%)): %; monocytes_abs (Monocytes (absolute)): 10^3/µL, 10^9/L, cells/µL; eosinophils_pct (Eosinophils (%)): %; eosinophils_abs (Eosinophils (absolute)): 10^3/µL, 10^9/L, cells/µL; basophils_pct (Basophils (%)): %; basophils_abs (Basophils (absolute)): 10^3/µL, 10^9/L, cells/µL; immature_granulocytes_pct (Immature granulocytes (%)): %; immature_granulocytes_abs (Immature granulocytes (absolute)): 10^3/µL, 10^9/L, cells/µL; nrbc_pct (Nucleated red blood cells (%)): %, /100 WBC; nrbc_abs (Nucleated red blood cells (absolute)): 10^3/µL, 10^9/L, cells/µL; total_cholesterol (Total cholesterol): mg/dL, mmol/L; ldl_c (LDL cholesterol): mg/dL, mmol/L; hdl_c (HDL cholesterol): mg/dL, mmol/L; non_hdl_c (Non-HDL cholesterol): mg/dL, mmol/L; triglycerides (Triglycerides): mg/dL, mmol/L; vldl_c (VLDL cholesterol): mg/dL, mmol/L; chol_hdl_ratio (Cholesterol/HDL ratio): ratio; ldl_hdl_ratio (LDL/HDL ratio): ratio; chol_hdl_risk (Cholesterol/HDL risk): ratio; ldl_hdl_risk (LDL/HDL risk): ratio; apob (Apolipoprotein B (ApoB)): mg/dL, g/L; lpa (Lipoprotein(a)): mg/dL, nmol/L; hba1c (HbA1c): %, mmol/mol; glucose (Glucose): mg/dL, mmol/L; tsh (TSH): mIU/L, µIU/mL; free_t4 (Free T4): ng/dL, pmol/L; free_t3 (Free T3): pg/mL, pmol/L; testosterone (Testosterone (total)): ng/dL, nmol/L; free_testosterone (Free testosterone): pg/mL, pmol/L; shbg (SHBG): nmol/L; oestradiol (Oestradiol): pg/mL, pmol/L; cortisol (Cortisol): µg/dL, nmol/L; insulin (Insulin): µIU/mL, pmol/L; creatinine (Creatinine): mg/dL, µmol/L; egfr (eGFR): mL/min/1.73m²; urea_nitrogen (Urea nitrogen (BUN)): mg/dL, mmol/L; cystatin_c (Cystatin C): mg/L; alt (ALT): U/L; ast (AST): U/L; ggt (GGT): U/L; ck (Creatine kinase (CK)): U/L; alp (Alkaline phosphatase (ALP)): U/L, IU/L; total_bilirubin (Total bilirubin): mg/dL, µmol/L; total_protein (Total protein): g/dL, g/L; albumin (Albumin): g/dL, g/L; sodium (Sodium): mmol/L, mEq/L; potassium (Potassium): mmol/L, mEq/L; chloride (Chloride): mmol/L, mEq/L; total_co2 (Carbon dioxide, total (CO2)): mmol/L, mEq/L; anion_gap (Anion gap): mmol/L, mEq/L; calcium (Calcium): mg/dL, mmol/L; hs_crp (hs-CRP): mg/L, mg/dL; crp (CRP): mg/L, mg/dL; vitamin_d (Vitamin D (25-OH)): ng/mL, nmol/L; vitamin_b12 (Vitamin B12): pg/mL, pmol/L; folate (Folate): ng/mL, nmol/L; magnesium (Magnesium (serum)): mg/dL, mmol/L; omega3_index (Omega-3 index): %. A ratio and the "risk" line a report prints beside it are separate markers, each recorded as printed. For a marker not on this list, leave marker out and give `name`.

tools.name: get_body_composition
tools.title: Body composition scans
tools.description: The athlete's body composition scans (DEXA) as recorded from their reports: total and regional fat, lean and bone mass, body fat percent, visceral fat, and whole-body bone density with the report's own percentiles. Values are as the report gave them, in the unit each field names. Read them back as measurements and nothing else: don't call a value healthy, ideal, high or low, don't suggest a body fat, weight or diet goal, and don't compare the athlete with anyone. Whole-body bone density is a measurement, not a diagnosis, and not a diagnostic bone density exam (those read the hip or spine and give T- or Z-scores); questions about it go to a clinician. Body Lab can't diagnose anything, and a scan never changes the training it prescribes. `comparableToPrevious` is false when the previous scan was done by another company or on another scanner model, which means a change may be the machine — it never means a change is real.

bmdGCm2.description: Whole-body bone mineral density, g/cm². A measurement from a whole-body scan, not a diagnostic bone density test, and not a T- or Z-score.

bmdAgeSexPercentile.description: The report's own comparison of the whole-body bone density with people of the same age and sex, 1-99, as printed. A comparison with a reference group, not a diagnosis.

bmdPeakSexPercentile.description: The report's own comparison with 30-year-olds of the same sex, 1-99, as printed. A comparison with a reference group, not a diagnosis.

comparableToPrevious.description: Whether the previous scan was done by the same company on the same scanner model, so the two read as one line. Null for the first scan.

differences.description: Why this scan isn't comparable with the previous one. Empty when it is, or when there's no previous scan.

items.description: What differs from the previous scan. Known values: provider, scanner_model. Treat unknown values as "other".

tools.name: record_body_composition
tools.title: Record a body composition scan
tools.description: Records one body composition scan (DEXA) from a report the athlete gives you — structured data from their scanning service, a PDF, a photo, or values they read out — exactly as printed. Prefer structured data over a photo where you have both. Before calling, read every value back to the athlete with its unit and get their yes: this can't edit or delete anything afterwards, and nothing else can edit a scan either; only the athlete can remove one, in Body Lab on the web. Masses are kilograms, density g/cm², volume cm³: convert from pounds yourself and say so in the read-back. Call get_body_composition first to see what's already recorded; one call per scan. It's all or nothing — if anything is refused (a scan already recorded for that date and provider, a region Body Lab doesn't know, fat plus lean plus bone not adding up to the total) nothing is saved, and the error lists each problem. Body Lab can't diagnose anything, and a scan never changes the training it prescribes.

scannedAt.description: When the scan was acquired, where the report gave a time.

source.description: How the scan was entered. Known values: manual. Treat unknown values as "other".

provider.description: The company or facility as the report prints it, e.g. BodySpec.

scannerModel.description: The scanner as the report prints it, e.g. "GE Lunar iDXA".

totalMassKg.description: Total mass, kilograms. Also recorded as a weigh-in, where it's given.

androidGynoidRatio.description: Android fat over gynoid fat, where the report gives it.

bmdGCm2.description: Whole-body bone mineral density, g/cm². A measurement from a whole-body scan, not a diagnostic bone density test, and not a T- or Z-score.

bmdAgeSexPercentile.description: The report's own comparison of the whole-body bone density with people of the same age and sex, 1-99, as printed. A comparison with a reference group, not a diagnosis.

bmdPeakSexPercentile.description: The report's own comparison with 30-year-olds of the same sex, 1-99, as printed. A comparison with a reference group, not a diagnosis.

regions.description: Each region the report measured, in the order the report's own list is read.

region.description: Which part of the body this row measures. Known values: left_arm, right_arm, left_leg, right_leg, trunk, android, gynoid. Treat unknown values as "other".

comparableToPrevious.description: Whether the previous scan was done by the same company on the same scanner model, so the two read as one line. Null for the first scan.

differences.description: Why this scan isn't comparable with the previous one. Empty when it is, or when there's no previous scan.

items.description: What differs from the previous scan. Known values: provider, scanner_model. Treat unknown values as "other".

__schema0.description: An instant: ISO-8601 with offset, e.g. 2026-09-13T06:30:00Z.

__schema5.description: Body fat percent of tissue, which excludes bone — the figure most reports headline.

__schema7.description: Bone mineral density, g/cm². A measurement, not a diagnosis.

__schema9.description: The bone area the density was measured over, cm².
